correctness.rationale: Independent orientations yield exact 1/2*(3/4)^(n-2) for E_{a,b}; shared first or second coordinate yields 1/4*(5/8)^(n-3). All other event pairs are bounded by chain 1/8*(1/2)^(n-3) or disjoint <=(9/16)^(n-4). Three distinct directed implications have probability at most 9/16 over fair independent endpoint bits, proved by graph-type classification and independently checked exhaustively; third Bonferroni term is bounded for n>=6. The exact explicit error bound proves the limit and two-cluster conditional law. A standalone checker exhaustively verified 5740 assertions; no finite check was used in place of the asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The original contribution is a second exponential 5/8 correction and a sharp asymptotic two-obstruction cluster law. One-event 3/4 probability and high-probability all-kings conclusion are known and explicitly not claimed. An inspected full-text 2022 kings paper contains a one-event product formula and prevalence thresholds, not the second-overlap formula. An inspected random-tournament correlation paper concerns unrestricted reachability, not two-step obstruction events. Comparisons with available published mathematical records did not show a stronger covering claim. Residual priority risk is recorded for inaccessible Maurer 1980 original and other historical work.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated reliability question is not merely whether all fair random tournament vertices are 2-kings with high probability, but the structure and sharp frequency of rare violations. The 5/8 second exponential term and conditional geometry of two failures isolate a specific two-event dependence mechanism, qualitatively beyond the classical 3/4 first-moment estimate. This can inform sharp finite-size probability approximation and local clustering analyses of the uncovered set; it is a structural rather than arbitrary numeric or definitional calculation.
